references.text: The Lord makes a distinction between Egypt and Israel, so that the plagues do not strike the land of Goshen where the Israelites live.
The Lord's promise to distinguish between the livestock of Israel and the livestock of Egypt is fulfilled in verse 6.
A similar pattern where the land of Goshen, where the Israelites lived, was spared from the plague.
The Lord makes a difference between the Egyptians and the Israelites during the plague of darkness.
The Lord sets a distinction between the Egyptians and Israel, so that Israel is protected.
The tenth plague also strikes the livestock of Egypt, while the firstborn of Israel are spared.
The psalm describes how God handed over the livestock of the Egyptians to pestilence and plague.
The Lord struck down all the firstborn in Egypt, including among the livestock.
Both illustrate God's ability to distinguish between Israel and Egypt in judgment, first over the livestock and later over the army.
Numbers 8 explains the theological significance of the event in Exodus (judgment on the firstborn/livestock) by linking it to the consecration of Israel's firstborn.
